title: Photo Duo 052 · 아워글래스 USSBBW × 아워글래스 SSBBW · 눕기 + 기대기 (머리 반대)
prompt:
Image format: a horizontal landscape-orientation photograph, 3:2 aspect ratio, wider than it is tall.

A photograph of TWO women on a low platform with a padded backrest at its right end, a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing else in the frame, the camera set close at platform level so the two of them fill the frame edge to edge, 50mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subjects: TWO real adult women, both far beyond any real person in size, lying head to toe in opposite directions — one reclining against the backrest at the right with her head at the right edge and rising to fill the full height of the picture, the other lying on her side along the front of the platform with her head at the left edge and her legs stretching back beneath the reclining woman's raised torso, their two bodies together filling the frame from edge to edge and top to bottom with almost no empty backdrop left.

Reclining woman, head at the right: a South Asian woman in her late 20s, rich warm brown skin with golden undertones, her face exactly the same tone as her body, a high top knot with loose strands. A colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size — the one place on her body where the outline pulls inward. Below it an immense mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and spills forward down the slope of her raised torso under its own weight, piling over her thighs and reaching toward her knees in three or four heavy rounded folds with deep creases between them, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, merging seamlessly into her sides, hips and thighs with no boundary anywhere, not pregnant. Colossal hips more than three times the width of that waistline and a gigantic rear, each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. Painted in Mexican Talavera — a glossy white tin glaze painted with cobalt blue, marigold yellow, terracotta orange and green rosettes, star medallions and scalloped borders, a thick cobalt border following every curve.

Lying woman, head at the left: a Korean woman in her late 40s, warm ivory skin with a golden undertone, her face exactly the same tone as her body, a wide round afro with a gold headband. A colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size — the one place on her body where the outline pulls inward. Below it a great mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and, even as she lies on her side, spills forward away from her body and hangs over the front edge of her torso, the lowest part sagging onto the platform in two or three heavy rounded folds with deep creases between them, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, merging seamlessly into her sides, hips and thighs with no boundary anywhere, not pregnant. Enormous round hips more than three times the width of that waistline, a gigantic rear, gigantic soft thighs, very thick soft arms. Her upper hip rises as a great rounded mound higher than her own shoulder, the underside hip and thigh flattening wide against the platform. Painted in Korean eunipsa silver inlay — a deep black ground with thick bright silver linework and fine lattice fills, a bold silver band following every deep crease, catching the light the way paint on skin does rather than like real metal.

The reclining woman's arms rest back on the platform behind her hips with the elbows out; the lying woman rests her head on her raised hand with that elbow planted behind her body, her other arm lifted clear on the top of her hip with the elbow raised. On both: real photographic skin with visible pores, creases where the flesh folds and faint stretch marks, no illustration finish, no CG sheen. The paint is pigment on living skin, distorting over every bulge and cracking where it folds, covering everything below the jaw with no bare skin left; their faces unpainted, the pattern fading out at the neck. Neither arm crosses in front of her own body or the other woman's, both faces toward the camera. Every fold keeps its own rounded outline with a deep crease between them, never one shapeless mass; arms, hands and legs in correct proportion. Both wear extreme platform stiletto heels with soles as tall as their ankle bones.

Horizontal 3:2 landscape-orientation photograph, wider than it is tall.
